gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-montagu-slab: Montagu Slab brings a sturdy, traditional text serif, with robust downstrokes and slender turns that stay moderate in contrast. And Conthrax goes the other way, drawing wide, geometric letters with unshaded strokes that look like one continuous thread.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-noto-serif-hentai: Sleek and geometric, Conthrax stretches its lowercase until the capitals barely stand above it. Noto Serif Hentaigana follows with a text serif whose strokes shift visibly but gently, giving the stiff heading a softer partner.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-ovo: Ovo reads like a classic, authoritative serif, its thick and thin strokes differing only slightly, like a soft pencil line with spacious curve endings. Conthrax, by contrast, holds pipe-cleaner-slim joins.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-domine: Raw and jagged, Disorder sets its big lowercase well apart with no swelling at the joins. Domine takes over with a dignified serif, its round letters carrying a faint nib-pressure shift that the heading never attempts.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-esteban: Chaotic is the first word for Disorder, whose oversized lowercase and pen-fixed curves sit apart with no swelling mid-curve, set against a refined serif. Esteban supplies the refinement.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-faustina: Faustina is a classic serif with bowls that thin gracefully and a c opening like a pair of pliers. Disorder does raw, constant-width pen lines best, while Faustina does measured, moderate contrast best.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-halant: Strokes pulled like solder through a nozzle define Disorder, with no swelling where curves meet stems and big lowercase spaced far apart. And Halant, a traditional text serif with towering x-height and outward-pointing terminals, adds a faint thick-thin shift beneath it.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-headland-one: Disorder draws its big lowercase with constant pen pressure and no swelling at the joins, glyphs spaced well apart. But Headland One, a dignified serif, adds heavier verticals like a tilted nib, and that gentle variation is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-hedvig-letters-se: Chaotic Disorder holds its joins at full thickness, with big lowercase and wide gaps between glyphs. Hedvig Letters Serif answers in a text serif with tall, sturdy lowercase, and that mild, friendly stroke contrast is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa reads sturdy and large, its tall lowercase and spilling counters framed by a mild, approachable serif contrast. Disorder's constant-width strokes would make that stretch feel rough and punchy.
